newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on importer deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on importer deals.

text.p: Start-of-the-week importer deals pushed the won to a lower close against the U.S. dollar in a quiet and tight-range trading on Monday, dealers said.
"The dollar opened strong on scheduled import account settlements," said a Hongkong Bank dealer. "But it moved in a narrow range on fewer-than-expected importer deals."
Dealers said a $15 million worth of government procurement deal also gave a strength on the dollar in early trading.
The won closed at 819.40 compared with its mid-rate of 818.60. After opening at 819.30, the local currency moved in a 819.60 and 818.90 range.
"With no specific factors to affect the market, the dollar is likely to hover around the 819.00 level for the time being," said a Shinhan Bank dealer.

He said dealers would sit on the sidelines as they were not sure how the market would react on expected dollar supplies from foreign funds into the local stock market, depositary receipts issue by South Korean banks and ballooning trade deficit.

The Hongkong Bank dealer forecast the dollar would range from 818.80 to 819.80 on Tuesday, while the Shinhan Bank dealer put it at 818.50-819.80. Tuesday's mid-rate is expected to be fixed at 819.30. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
